#3972. Diablo 4's next season won't have any new mechanics or a new theme because all the focus is on Lord of Hatred

If you don't intend to buy the Lord of Hatred expansion, the next season in Diablo 4 won't be as exciting as you'd expect.

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

#3970. Pikmin 4 Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy X Tetris 99 Event Announced, Unlock A Special Theme

Nintendo has announced a Pikmin 4 Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy crossover for its addictive online battle royale game Tetris 99.

It's taking place between 26th November 2026 and 30th November 2026. During this time, you'll be able to unlock a special theme when you earn 100 event points. Here is Nintendo's official announcement, and you can see the new theme in action in the video above.

"The Tetris® 99 58th MAXIMUS CUP event runs from 11pm PT on November 26 to 10:59pm PT on November 30. To participate, you’ll need to be a Nintendo Switch Online member* and play the Tetris 99 online mode during the event period. You’ll earn event points based on your placement in each match. Once you’ve accumulated a total of 100 event points, a new theme will unlock, featuring art, music and Tetrimino designs inspired by the Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy game for the Nintendo Switch 2 system!"

You can find out more about the new Switch 2 Edition of Pikmin 4 and Dandori Academy in our review here on Nintendo Life:

Mini Review Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy (Switch 2) - Pleasant But Perplexingly Piecemeal

Review Tetris 99 (Switch) - A Revolutionary Take On A Puzzle Classic

#3969. Poll: So, What Do You Think Of GTA 6?

It's early days, but let us know your thoughts so far

We've been talking GTA 6 all week here at Pure Xbox, but now it's time for the community to take centre stage! We want to know what you think about the new Grand Theft Auto based on what you've played so far.

It's no secret that GTA 6 has been reviewing better than pretty much any game in existence since its release a few days ago. As things stand, it sits alongside the original Ocarina of Time as the best game ever made on Metacritic!

We helped contribute to that with our "Outstanding" 10/10 review score here at Pure Xbox:

Review GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

This is going to dominate your life for months!

I have no doubt that it's a 10/10 in my mind, but is it the joint-best video game of all time? That's a much harder statement to make, and I think it's going to need months and years before we can really evaluate it in that regard.

It should also be pointed out that despite the reviewers heaping praise on it, and the Xbox and PlayStation store ratings being extremely high for GTA 6 right now, the game's user score on Metacritic is surprisingly low - so clearly there are plenty of people who aren't so hot on what they've played and/or seen so far.

We're well aware that many Pure Xbox users are probably just a few hours into their experience with GTA 6 so far though, and therefore it's very early days as things stand. We don't want you to give a definitive verdict on the game down below, but just let us know your initial thoughts and whether you're satisfied or not with your purchase.

Also tell us what you think of the vibe compared to GTA 4 and GTA 5 - we're very curious about that!

What did you pick in the poll above? Let us know in the comments section down below.

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

Gears E-Day and GTA 6 are two very different experiences, so they're not really easy to compare. However, if we're talking purely about fun and action, I think Gears E-Day comes out on top, and honestly by quite a large margin.

Everything feels more condensed in Gears E-Day: the story, the action sequences, the pacing, and the overall presentation. As a result, the experience delivers stronger and more immediate sensations. Of course, that intensity comes over a shorter period of time, which is expected given that it's a semi-open-world game.

Even from a technical and graphical standpoint, I was more impressed by Gears E-Day. That said, context matters: GTA 6 is a massive open-world game, so it's only natural that it doesn't have the same level of polish and visual density as a more focused, semi-open-world title like Gears E-Day.

#3968. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.8 is refreshing your team comps with a new mechanic, and the game is coming to Steam

Zenless Zone Zero will soon become the first HoYoverse game to make its way to Steam, though we wish we had more details.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a new Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

#3966. Missed something on your first go around The Blood of Dawnwalker? I've got good news, as next week's update adds in new game plus

A big part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 update next week that adds in a new game plus mode.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

In any case, the update goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration."

Overall, a bit of a smaller update compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something important or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests."

#3965. Genshin Impact Luna 7 brings us the first playable Hexenzirkel as things take a turn in Sumeru

Genshin Impact's Luna 7 update will kick off a new Archon Quest chapter, and deliver some interesting new additions to the playable roster.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a new Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter quickly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Company, is the second new character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One new gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

#3964. From 2D to 3D and back to 2D again, the original platforming classic Super Meat Boy returns with a slick remaster complete with new levels and too many old saws

Earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a new dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

What is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a big new lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff."

If the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

There's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an update there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as big a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the new one on Steam.

#3963. Three Games Are Confirmed For Xbox Game Pass To End The Month (November 24-27)

Here's what's on the way to close out the month

With only a handful of days left to go, November is well and truly coming to a close. Before we whip out the Xmas deccies, we've still got another three Xbox Game Pass titles to come over the next few days.

Starting off with XGP Premium members being treated to not just one, but two new additions to the mid-tier subscription. MOTORSLICE is making the move from Ultimate, whilst Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 is joining all but Essential on November 24.

The only "day one" game is coming just three days later, when Arkheron, a "fast-paced, clip-worthy team PvP game" joins Ultimate and PC Game Pass. It looks like a vibrant one if MOBAs are your cuppa.

Admittedly, it's a bit of a quiet end to November, but we'll leave you with a closer look at each of these games below.

On this page: Three Games Are Confirmed For Xbox Game Pass To End The Month (November 24-27)

Parkour through the ruins of a megastructure, climb massive bosses, and hunt down every construction equipment in this slice of life action-adventure with immaculate vibes.

Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 now includes ‘Butcher’s Banquet’: a major expansion which introduces an entirely new and expansive region - The Temple - complete with all-new objectives and some of your most deadly contracts, yet.

Arkheron is a fast-paced, clip-worthy team PvP game where the items you equip dynamically change how you play. Grab your friends, loot Relics that change your build mid-fight, and climb a haunted Tower floor by floor. If you've played a shooter or a MOBA, your aim and your instincts already work here. The builds, the counters, the hundred ways a fight can turn all boils down to your adaptability and skill.

@Schonks it matters to me. I enjoy hearing how people feel about new releases or the value they’re finding on the platform. I never know what I’ll learn from them until I read it.

I personally don't see any problem with sharing opinions over here, whether we agree with them or not. After all, that's the whole point of having a community, isn't it? Keep 'em coming, @Fiendish-Beaver!

(By the way, I love GP and see a lot of value in it, though I'm skeptical about its future.)

I think there is a lot to love about Games Pass, @Jean_McClane, though these days it is not for me. I prefer those big AAA single player experiences, along with the occasional AA/AA+ games. I am not into the smaller Indie games, which is essentially what Game Pass offers more than anything these days. I also prefer to buy my games, even first-party games, so I don't get a lot of value out of Game Pass myself, but that is not to say that it does not offer superb value for those that enjoy Indie games or are not in a position to buy all the games like I am.

Honestly though, I am only expressing my personal view point. I am not telling anyone else what they should be doing. That is for them to decide. However, if you think about it, if we only were allowed to post what would be seen as positive view points, then how would we know what people really think? And should the bosses at Microsoft read these forums, then is it not better that they know where their community sits?

I know I am one of the first to call out Xbox, and what I perceive to be the problems it is facing, but it is honestly brought from a place of love for Xbox. It is my home, and I want it to do really, really well. So, even if I seem negative about Xbox, I am not being so because I am rubbing my hands in glee at the thought of it failing.

Anyway, I apologise for giving such a long response. Thank you for your kind words, and have a good day...

@Fiendish-Beaver, thank you for sharing. I totally get your point and I must say, I agree with a lot of what you said.

My backlog is huge, and GP helps me try games beyond demos - such as Valor Mortis - to decide if I'll buy them or not. I love indie games by the way, but I usually buy them on Steam.

Regarding positive vs. negative feedback, I also believe different opinions are what move things forward. If we agree on everything, there's definitely something wrong and life would be way too boring.

I consider myself an Xbox person - I even sold my PS5 - and I'll stick to their ecosystem as long as they provide value. I'm optimistic (maybe I shouldn't be) about Helix, so I'm holding off on buying any games until I decide whether I'll stick with them or stay on PC and Switch 2 only.

Xbox has a long road ahead, and if Helix is even half of what they're promising (a hybrid PC and console), they might have a shot against the almighty greedy blue.

At the end of the day, we just want a stable and sustainable gaming console, and titles fun enough that we can turn our brains off (or totally fry them).

My turn: apologies for the long response and GG!!!

My real worry about Helix is that it will be too prohibitively expensive to sell in sufficient numbers to succeed, @Jean_McClane. Xbox enthusiasts, such as myself, will still take the plunge regardless, but those that expect consoles to cost similar to what they did back when the PS5 and Series consoles released, are going to be sorely disappointed. However, I don't think they will just be disappointed, but if Helix is too expensive they will also do one of three things; leave gaming completely (although I think that will be a very smaller percentage). Or two, maybe look elsewhere (PS6 or Switch 2). Or stick with the current generation consoles, which I think will be supported for the entirety of the next generation.

I believe a lot of the future success for Xbox (in terms of consoles) depends very much on not only how much Helix costs, but how much more than the PS6 it costs. If there is more than £500 between them, then I think there exists the real possibility of a lot of current Xbox gamers leaving for PlayStation, and that the number that do will be on a sliding scale; so the smaller the gap between Helix and the PS6 the fewer people will swap over, and vice versa.

If Helix is £1000 then I think it should be okay up against a similar costing PS6. If it is £1500 and the PS6 is £1000, then I think it will be in trouble. If the gap is bigger than that then it could be disastrous.

I have a decent gaming PC, so I am sorted in that regard, but I actually have an aversion to gaming on it. I much prefer the simplicity of gaming on a console, so even though I will be getting Helix (and the PS6) I will be getting it as my primary gaming console, and probably not be using its PC capabilities at all.

I think with the current generation favouring Sony roughly 3/1 that Sony may well decide to subsidise their consoles because they know they can monetise their gamers to recoup that money, whereas with Xbox having far fewer gamers, the chances of Microsoft subsidising Helix is much less. That could exacerbate the margin of difference between the cost of the PS6 and Helix, which could end up driving still more people into the open arms of Sony.

It's going to be fascinating to watch and see how each consoles does during the next generation. I am hoping for the best for Xbox, but am prepared for it to get quite hairy...!

#3962. ICYMI: Here's Another Look At The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time amiibo For Switch 2

In September, Nintendo revealed it would be releasing two new amiibo in 2027 based on characters from the Zelda: Ocarina of Time Switch 2 remake.

This includes Young Link (and Navi) and Young Zelda. Some photos of these amiibo at conventions are now appearing online. If you haven't already seen them, here's another look via the amiibo subreddit:

These same amiibo have also been spotted at other game events recently, with more photos of them surfacing on social media. GameSpot shared a closer look at these amiibo last month, alongside the limited-edition Switch 2 and Pro Controller.

The exact release date for these amiibo hasn't been confirmed just yet, so when we hear more, we'll let you know. As for the price, they'll set you back $24.99 USD (or your regional equivalent). You'll be able to unlock some special content with them in the remake. This includes masks based on Link and Zelda's original appearances in Ocarina of Time on the N64.

You can find out more about amiibo and what exactly they do in Ocarina of Time in our guides here on Nintendo Life. Nintendo also recently released the final Kirby Air Riders amiibo.

#3961. Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

With the 10th anniversary of Mystic Messenger nearly upon us, the dating sim has inexplicably begun issuing wide-spread bans for its most active players.

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

The message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a new automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

#3960. Silent Hill, Fatal Frame Inspire This Promising New PS5 Horror Game

You're probably describing at least half of the horror genre when you list Silent Hill and Fatal Frame as two of your main inspirations, but Ugly Within has cut through the crowded space with a reveal at The Horror Game Awards 2026.

It is in development for PS5, Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, with no release window confirmed yet. Catch it in action in the trailer above.

You play as two characters: Shu, a boy who can see into the past, and Reiko, an exorcist. It sounds like you'll be looking into a family history and confronting the ghost that has haunted it. Shu is a more stealthy character who avoids the supernatural and solves puzzles, while Reiko confronts the ghosts and exorcises them.

Shu and Reiko face the horrors of the Kamata estate in very different ways. Shu survives by staying unseen, moving through the house in silence and piecing together its secrets through visions of what once happened within its walls. Reiko meets the darkness head-on, confronting the entities that haunt the estate and driving them out through exorcism. But Shu's gift comes with a cruel limit: his visions reveal what happened to the people who came before, yet nothing he sees can be undone.

There is a touch of jank to the footage released so far, but the production quality overall appears to be really quite high. A lot like Perceptum, I think this one of the indie horror titles you need to keep an eye on.

#3959. Congratulations to people who feel mean shooting random NPCs, because GTA 6 tries "to provide mechanisms that encourage" empathy

When you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a new interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

"Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a new interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to."

I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

In any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

#3958. Forza Horizon 6 explodes on Steam even before it's officially out

Forza Horizon 6 looks to have easily delivered the most successful launch for any game in the series on PC, with record-breaking player numbers.

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated launches, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

#3957. Rasen, out in early access now, is a PvP focused take on Dark Souls that borrows one of fighting games' best techy tricks

The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being said, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just launched into early access.

To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things. For one, it looks more like it leans a tad towards Sekiro with a blades-only kind of affair, whether that be big or small. And blades a plenty they have, ranging from your classic sword, to scythes, to halberds and all sorts. It's a much flashier looking affair too, with fancy slashing effects that seem to buff moves and a pace that seems much faster than Souls games tend to be.

You can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat! And best of all, unusually for a 3D arena fighter, it has rollback netcode. For those unfamiliar, and to try and explain it simply, this is essentially a bit of tech you'll find in predominantly 2D fighting games that predicts every possible input you could make in a given moment, helping to reduce lag time and allow for tighter matches (and less rage quitting).

That's a bit harder to do in a 3D environment given that you have a lot more options at your disposal when it comes to movement, so if it works that's some impressive stuff! And we could all quite easily find out together, as a demo for Rasen is available to try out. Or, alternatively, you can just pick it up whole hog on Steam right now, as it's available in early access.

#3956. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.3 will take us deeper into the World in Canvas and make Mortenax Blade playable

Honkai: Star Rail's next big outing will see the continuation of the Planarcadia story, and it's going to be with us soon.

HoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a new chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

While the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can plan where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

There’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

#3955. GTA 6 Glitch Unlocks The FPS On Xbox Series X|S, But With Multiple Drawbacks

It's a bug related to Quick Resume on Series X|S

Update [Mon 23rd Nov 2026, 6:52pm]: The folks over at Digital Foundry have also now taken a look at this, concluding that the unlocked FPS is still too inconsistent to make an official version viable as things stand.

Their analysis is pretty fascinating though, and you can watch it up above.

News Digital Foundry Analyses Whether GTA 6 Could Benefit From 40FPS On Xbox Series X

"A 40fps mode with VRR could still make sense"

Original Story: If there's anything we could add to GTA 6 as things stand, it'd be an official 60FPS mode. That's obviously not possible right now due to how demanding the game is on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S hardware, even in the case of the PS5 Pro.

Interestingly though, over the weekend, players have discovered the ability to activate what some are calling a "60FPS Glitch" or "60FPS Bug" on Xbox consoles, forcing the game to unlock its FPS and run at a higher frame rate than it's actually supposed to.

Someone called Meowwie64 on Reddit appears to have found this, and here's what they did to activate it:

Now, as mentioned, there are multiple drawbacks here. The first one is that the glitch speeds up most aspects of the game, making it run faster than intended (and look like it's in fast-forward mode!). This is obviously not an ideal way to enjoy GTA 6, and serves as an immediate deal-breaker in my view.

Another one is that reaching 60FPS is pretty much impossible under normal gameplay circumstances. If you're driving down a highway, for example, you're likely only going to get around 35-40FPS at max, with 60FPS and above being saved for situations that require no graphical intensity whatsoever.

And finally, it should be noted that GTA 6 was never intended to be run this way on Xbox Series X|S, and therefore you could run into all sorts of issues - crashes, bugs, maybe even your console overheating. That last one is unlikely, but the game has been specifically built to run at 30FPS on these machines, so it's not worth pushing it in our view.

We'll leave you with some footage of this glitch running on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S down below (courtesy of the always-excellent Fuzion Xbox Testing), and prepare for it to be officially fixed in an upcoming GTA 6 update.

Talking Point How Often Are You Willing To Play Games At 30FPS?

#3954. Forage and fight for ingredients in a magical 1960s Italy and whip up some tasty meals Cooking Mama style in The Snackbar at the End of the World

If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

First up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

The other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only announced this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.

#3953. Monopoly Go x The Simpsons crossover is almost here

After a long wait and exhaustive leaks, the highly-anticipated Simpsons event will finally arrive in Monopoly Go very soon, alongside new content.

Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.

The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a new animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

The developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:

Episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a new Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

If you're excited to jump in tomorrow, be sure to check out these Free Monopoly Go Dice Links before you dive into the new content.

#3950. The Sunday Papers

The Sunday Papers is our weekly roundup of great writing about (mostly) videogames from across the web.

While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promise Mascot Agency.

Deep in a drawer, you discover a sour-smelling binder full of extracts from an ancient and all but indecipherable dispute over the discovery of "generative AI" in something called "Big Walk". The stakes are long-buried, but many of the individual pieces of writing are lively. Here is Bruno Dias noting in passing that "one of the harms of the 'AI' political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless." Here is a professorial interjection from Brendan Keogh calling on the warring parties to recognise when "critiques of generative AI are actually just deflected critiques of the capitalist relations of technology and labour". Here is Mike Cook arguing that "what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'." Here is a ticker tape message from Hannah Nicklin observing that "if your radical position doesn’t have room for transformation it will not be safe until it contains just you".

A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

Peering at the weirdly white and opaque windowpanes, you realise there are intricate equations traced in the condensation. It appears to be a post-mortem for a "post-cosy" game called Danchi Days, in which developer Melos Han-Tani discusses wishlist conversion rates and the problem of not fitting neatly into any recognisable genre.

A snowglobe stands on a mantelpiece, the flakes still orbiting a miniature washtub as though the object had been recently shaken, even though the chamber has clearly been abandoned for decades. You put it to your ear, anticipating the faint jingle of Xmas bells. Instead, you are almost deafened by a screeching guitar chord. Here is Erin Keane to explain.

Next to the snowglobe on the mantelpiece, there's a souvenir shop conch shell, polished to a high sheen. You put that to your ear, hoping to catch the soothing shuffle of surf on shingle, and a disembodied voice tells you to piss off. Tim Sniffen has some thoughts about gentrification, and why only he should be allowed to do it.

Again, one of these mystic artefacts hides the key to your release from the suffocating stillness of Sunday Afternoon. Which will you choose? Or have you, perhaps, brought a sorcerous teleportation device of your own? Please share. Here is Joanna Newsom's Cosmia to help you think.

#3948. Tiny Bookshop Sells 1 Million Copies, New DLC Expansion Announced

Tiny Bookshop, the charming indie title in which you take on the role of bookseller in a quaint seaside resort, has officially sold surpassed 1 million copies sold across PC, Switch, PS5, Xbox, iOS, and Android since its launch in August 2025.

To celebrate, publisher Skystone Games and developer neoludic have announced a new DLC expansion launching on 5th December 2026: Arts & Crafts.

The expansion opens up two new locations – Puffin Primary and the Artist Quarter – while also adding 24 new wagon parts, over 30 new decor items, new quests, and a mystery surrounding a stolen painting. Ooh. It's more of the same, then, albeit with seemingly less emphasis on the act of selling books.

That's all the information we have to go on right now, but more is promised very soon – and we should hope so, given how close the release date is!

We awarded Tiny Bookshop a score of 8/10 in our review, calling it "a fun little experience whether you’re into reading or not". If you enjoyed it, then it might be worth keeping an eye out for the new expansion.

#3947. "We've finally reached this milestone": Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP kicks off open beta after around six years preparing for cybermayhem

"Let's see how the project handles real player traffic"

After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics."

"Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "New features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!"

According to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

For info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

#3946. Rumour: LA Noire 2 Is Rockstar's Next Game

Okay, you'll have to stick with me for this one because it's going to take some explaining...

So, all the way back in 2023, a supposed leak on the GTAForums (please beware of potential GTA 6 spoilers if you click this link) attracted relatively little attention. At the time, there was no way to prove that any of it was legit.

The "leak" in question revealed Rockstar's schedule, with the original poster claiming that a sequel to LA Noire would be the developer's next game, after GTA 6, and it was targeting a 2030 release.

The reason it's being brought again almost three years later — chiefly via Reddit — is because as it turns out, the leaker did get a number of details about GTA 6 correct. Most notably, they managed to provide surprisingly solid info on the game's multiple endings — and they'd obviously be quite difficult to predict without some kind of insider knowledge.

To be clear, not everything in the "leak" has ended up being correct. It's a little hit and miss, but then things can change in the space of two and a half years or so; it's possible that these inaccurate details were legit at or before the time of posting.

I think the deciding factor for the believers here is that Rockstar moving on to a new LA Noire would make some sense.

Assuming it's in line with the first game, you would think that it would be a much smaller production than something like Red Dead Redemption 3 — even with the tech and engine refinements the company has made with GTA 6.

Plus, there is some LA Noire DNA in both Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 6; environmental and NPC interactions are key parts of Rockstar's most recent releases, and they arguably stem from LA Noire's investigative gameplay loop.

It's also worth remembering that after LA Noire's original developer Team Bondi was closed in 2011 (with Rockstar retaining the rights to LA Noire itself), its founder Brendan McNamara would go on to establish a new outfit called Video Games Deluxe.

The Australian studio crafted LA Noire: The VR Case Files years later, and even took over post-launch support for GTA: The Trilogy following its incredibly shoddy launch. Video Games Deluxe was then acquired by Rockstar in 2025, and it was renamed Rockstar Australia. Hmmm.

So some of this stuff seems to line up — but I don't think there's quite enough evidence here to nail the suspect. I mean, er, put your full trust in that original leak. Still, I wouldn't say no to another LA Noire.

Would you love to see an LA Noire sequel? Feel free to doubt all of this in the comments section below.

#3945. "Nobody was hurt" in shooting near Clockwork Revolution devs InXile Entertainment's office, the Xbox-owned studio and police confirm

"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is currently being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

"Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson said in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

"We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile said in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

InXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

Since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power."

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

Who's up for some new release dates for Xbox Game Pass titles? Well, we've got two for you today, both of which are scheduled to join the service in early 2027.

First up is Nubby's Number Factory, a funky-looking plinko-style roguelike which has you working in a numbers factory and trying to stop the sun from exploding. Makes sense, right? Well, it's on the way to XGP on January 14, 2027.

Alongside that comes Mr Magpie's Harmless Card Game. The spooky deckbuilder had already been announced during October's ID@Xbox showcase, but now we have an official release date of February 18, 2027.

These games will be joining an already impressive batch of early 2027 Xbox Game Pass releases, battling for attention amongst the likes of Persona 4 Revival, Stranger Than Heaven, Tropico 7, and Fable.

So, here's a closer look at the two games confirmed for Xbox Game Pass in Early 2027:

On this page: Two More Games Confirmed For Xbox Game Pass In Early 2027

A plinko-style roguelike where you work at a number factory. Launch your spherical friend, Nubby, down a pegboard to make bigger and bigger numbers! But beware, if you fail to meet your number quota, the sun will explode.

A surreal corporate horror deckbuilder where you gamble your life for cash, dodge murderous JERRY cards, and “maximise synergies” to climb the company ladder in Mr Magpie’s office nightmare.

#3942. Blade Runner 2099 lands positive Rotten Tomatoes score as first reviews praise its "stunning" world-building

The new Prime Video series has mostly been a hit with critics

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Blade Runner 2099 has been a hit with critics, landing a respectable Rotten Tomatoes score ahead of its Prime Video release. The new series, which will debut in full on Wednesday, November 25, is currently sitting at 72% on the review aggregation site, based on 36 reviews.

Starring Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer, the new entry in the beloved franchise is set following a Replicant uprising, which places Replicants in charge of humans. Yeoh's Olwen and Schafer's Cora team up to try and stop the potential collapse of their city by finding a young runaway harboring key secrets.

The eight-episode show is dropping in full and early reviews have been positive. Praising Schafer and Yeoh in the lead roles, many have called it a gripping adventure, even if it doesn't touch the level of the two movies.

Indie Wire's Ben Travers wrote: "Blade Runner 2099 may not be as exquisite as its predecessors (and it won't likely win over audiences who aren't already fans), but it nails the franchise's aura – and builds one awesome world."

"Elevated by stunning visuals and a pair of dynamic performances, the series proves that even with humanity on the back foot, there are still ways to find empathy in the desolation," adds William Goodman at The Wrap.

The Telegraph's Patrick Smith gives it four stars, writing: "Set 80 years after Ridley Scott's original, Amazon’s labyrinthine sci-fi series is a tour-de-force of meticulous world-building."

The Hollywood Reporter's Angie Han was less impressed. "This Blade Runner might look the part, might act the part, might even be trying very hard to be the part as best as it can," they wrote. "But you don't need a Voight-Kampff test to see it hasn't quite managed to replicate the soul."

"Its visual ambition is astounding," Time Magazine's Judy Berman agrees. "Yet that bleak beauty continues to obscure the personalities of its protagonists and the shape of their society."

For more, check out our Blade Runner timeline and our round-up of the best shows on Prime Video.

#3939. GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty to 2022 Rockstar Games breach which the company claim cost them $5 million

Hacker was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

Kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the company contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely shows anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

#3938. Mini Review: KuloNiku: Bowl Up! (Switch 2) - A Satisfying, Tactile Cooking Sim

I have a real soft spot for games that simulate cooking. A strange thing given my aversion to crafting mechanics, but cooking? I could do that all day.

KuloNiku: Bowl Up! Is right up my alley, then. Developed by Gamebir Studio, it sees you take on the role of a new meatball restaurant owner. Your job is to pay close attention to your customers’ orders to ensure maximum satisfaction, thus increasing your reputation and revenue.

Your workstation is separated into sections, and you’ll need to tab between them to complete your order quickly and accurately. Someone orders a Classic Bowl with extra chilli? You’ll need to grab your bowl, go straight to the cooking pan, add three meatballs and one noodle nest, then tab over to the chopping board, grab your chilli and finely slice it. Once that’s added, tab back to your pan, chuck the meatballs and noodles into your bowl, add a ladle of broth, then go to your seasoning station. Add a blob of sweet soy sauce and your cutlery, then serve.

If you nail your customer’s order, they’ll shower you with praise and chuck a few coins into your tip jar. Get something wrong and they’ll let you know, but there generally isn’t any major penalty. If you really mess up, your customer may ask for a full refund, lowering your reputation.

As you complete orders and memorise your recipes, you’ll complete tasks a lot faster. It’s such a tactile experience, too. Using an on-screen cursor, you have to manually select each ingredient while having direct control over your knife when slicing through veg. It serves as the perfect game for mouse controls on Switch 2, giving accuracy that feels otherwise limited via analogue controls. In handheld, the touchscreen can be used to cycle through dialogue but not for cooking.

In addition to cooking, you can decorate your restaurant, visit the shop to purchase new ingredients and items, and nurture your relationships with NPCs during your time off. This usually involves visiting new areas of the neighbourhood and engaging in dialogue. Each area is a static background, so don’t go expecting to wander around; the focus will remain on your conversations.

Finally, you have Meatball Brawls, or ‘Meatbrawls’. These are scheduled competitions in which you showcase your cooking skills to be judged against an opponent. You’ll need to be on your toes with this, as the judges and audience throw in fresh requests in the heat of battle, forcing you to reconsider your flow to accommodate new ingredients. Win the brawl, and you’ll gain an even stronger reputation.

Overall, I found all of the activities outside of the kitchen to be fun enough, but I was constantly eager to get back to cooking. If the game is missing a key ingredient, it’s a mode in which you just cook recipes over and over. The main campaign limits you to just three customers per in-game day, which is a shame. Otherwise, it’s a great time for budding restaurateurs.

There's never been a better time to be a fan of The Legend of Zelda. Not only did the legendary gaming franchise celebrate its 40th anniversary earlier in 2026, but the recent Ocarina of Time remake has become one of 2026's best-selling games. Why not celebrate the franchise, then, with a Zelda gift?

Owing to its longevity, Legend of Zelda gifts take many forms, and so there are many different items you can choose from. Whether you're looking for something for yourself, or know a Zelda fan who'll be hoping for a gift this holiday season, there's plenty to pick from.

To help guide you to some worthy items, here are a few items Legend of Zelda products which would make wonderful gifts. I've omitted games themselves — hopefully, you or recipient already owns these — and have picked a selection to encompass all kinds of Zelda gifts.

All of these items are in stock, at the time of writing, and some could become cheaper in the Black Friday gaming deals in the run-up to November's end.

While the official Zelda-themed Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller has been selling out pretty consistently, many reliable third-party controller makers have also been creating The Legend of Zelda controllers for the Switch 2, and most of them are readily available to buy online.

PowerA is one such company, as its Decayed Master Sword wireless controller is easy to pick up and, as a bonus, costs less than the official model since it's not a Pro controller. It has plenty of additional buttons on the front and back, hall effect sticks and a 30-hour battery life.

It's a very similar model to the main PowerA Advantage Nintendo Switch 2 Controller, but with a few extra buttons and tweaks to improve it from the base model. We gave that standard controller a mixed review, but it's very affordable, and the upgrades to the Decayed Master Sword model should offset most of them. The real advantage, though is simply that it's a Zelda controller which you can actually buy online.

Hardware nerds unite, sign up to our free tech newsletter for a weekly digest of the hottest new tech, the latest gadgets on the test bench, and much more from the team at GamesRadar+.

Of the two The Legend of Zelda-themed Lego sets, this Ocarina of Time set is the perfect one. Not only is it far cheaper than the Great Deku Tree kit, but it's more readily available in stock.

The set gets you a little minifigure of Link, Zelda and Ganandorf, and a giant Ganon which dominates the kit. The rest is made up of a diorama of the titular final battle, including loads more icons from Ocarina of Time. It's designed more as a display model than a play kit, but it has over 1,000 pieces and will fit on smaller shelf spaces.

The Ocarina of Time Final Battle Lego kit has had spotty availability in the past, but it's getting easier to pick up from a range of outlets. More Lego Zelda sets are expected to release in 2027, but for holiday gifts this year, the Final Battle set is the best of Zelda fans.

There are several books which have been written to celebrate the Legend of Zelda franchise, but perhaps the best for fans is this official Nintendo Encyclopedia, published in 2018 by Dark Horse Comics.

This is the third in a series of three, following a history book and an art book, and it's the ultimate lore compendium for fans of the franchise. It has over 300 pages full of information on the universe of the games; character relationship trees, the history of weapons and artifacts, character design evolutions, and much more.

A work like The Legend of Zelda Encyclopedia is a perfect coffee table book if you're a fan of the franchise, but it'd also make for a wonderful gift for someone who's gotten into the games more recently. It'll help them understand how the faces and places they've become acquainted with begun, and how they fit into the wider world of the Zelda franchise.

#3935. Intel are being sued for "misleading" investors about "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory" thanks to AI-fuelled price hikes

Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

The lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation". In a press release, they say they've filed suit on behalf of anybody who bought Intel stock from July 23rd to October 29th this year.

The suit claims that Intel neglected to tell investors that falling PC and component sales were having a "materially greater negative impact" on their third financial quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Groupresults than Intel had previously stated – to the tune of "hundreds of millions of dollars" in revenue shrinkage, compared to the previous quarter, with the situation still expected to "worsen".

They also accuse the company of keeping schtum about the aforesaid "massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", together with the fact that "any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described above."

Finally, they say Intel bosses have failed to disclose that they're struggling to procure an adequate supply of substrates – that is, materials used to create the base layer of chips, circuit boards and similar components. As such, the lawyers claim, Intel couldn't "ramp up production to meet data center CPU demand even if the Company chose to divert production resources because of a slowdown in PC-related sales."

Once the Godzilla of personal computing, Intel haven't been having a brilliant few years. Back in 2024, they recorded a multi-billion dollar quarterly loss, pushing then-CEO Pat Gelsinger to resign. As regards sales of gaming PCs, they've fallen behind AMD, though they've reportedly taken some ground back recently as regards desktop CPUs. As regards graphics cards, they have long been dwarfed by Nvidia.

Any Intel investor who wants a piece of that lawsuit has until January 12th 2027 to sign up as a lead plaintiff – that is, a court appointee who represents the interests of other class members. As regards us little people who don't buy stock in huge technology corporations, all this merely continues the weird existential crisis wrought upon 'traditional' gaming and computing hardware by the feckless quest to sell a better chatbot.

Update [Mon 23rd Nov 2026, 2:50pm]: Rockstar has now published the patch notes for GTA 6 PS5 update 01.002.002. Here they are in full:

Guide GTA 6: Patch Notes - All Updates & Fixes (November 2026)

Original Story: Rockstar Games has today published the first GTA 6 post-launch update on PS5, bringing its open worlder up to version number 01.002.002.

It's a small 603.8MB patch on PS5, and a 1.6GB download on Xbox Series X|S consoles. However, you might not be able to download it right away on PS5. It appears the developer is utilising a rollout system where owners of the game receive the patch in waves.

According to Rockstar dataminer Tex2, the update is live right now for 33% of GTA 6 owners on PS5. Another third of the title's userbase gets the patch in another few hours, and then everyone will have it by the end of the day. This is apparently to avoid server overload.
