So far, I’d say Witcher 3’s a bigger artistic statement, but GTA6 is a FAR bigger technical achievement from what I’ve played so far. I need more time in the game to make definitive statements, but I think the game will be sort of divisive with the nerds in the long run because of how many people are saying “it’s better than everything ever, quit game development.” I mean, we literally had a similar wave with Clair Obscur last year. All the same things were said about Baldur’s Gate 3. This kind of thing sort of causes retaliation as much as celebration these days.

I'm not trying to be disrespectful here, so please understand that, but you do have to wonder what other developers could do with an £800 million budget and an allowance of 8 to 10 years to complete their game.

I'm not trying to put Rockstar down here. I have not played GTA 6 (and may not), but the truth is that most developers are given half the time that Rockstar took to make GTA 6, and also a third of the budget at most. Instead of pushing boundaries, as Rockstar have done, most developers are looking for ways to cut corners and get their games out as soon as possible.

Honestly, if a developer such as Larian or CD Red were afforded the time and the money to make the game they really wanted, I am sure we would be equally amazed at what they produce. The truth is, when you look at what Larian and CD Red achieve with a fraction of the budget and half the time, then it makes you realise what technical marvels their games turn out to be.

When you see how much money GTA 6 has made (a return of something like 8 times the amount the game cost to make) you do have to wonder whether any other developer is actually in a position to do something similar, and the answer is probably not...

@Fiendish-Beaver I don’t disagree with your statement in many ways.

However, on the subject of CDPR, with Cyberpunk 2077, every AAA and some even AA studios could absolutely deliver what they have.

They started “work” on Cyberpunk 2077 as far back as 2010-2011 if memory serves.

It was then in and out of development, until about 2016 when it was an all hands on deck approach. Not the start of development, simply at that point many more in the studio working on actively producing a working title.

Then, release came, again, I believe was around 2020. So say at that point 9-10 years of development, with 4 or just under/over years of true entire studio development of some sort.

Yet, they released a game so bad in its basic coding and functionality, that they claimed they weren’t aware of, to then claim they were aware of, then had journalists embargo to not tell of this until launch/very close to launch.

They then offered mass refunds, one of the industries first physical and digital refunds of its kind. Where even I sent them my disc back to their office directly and got a refund.

It then took them up until shall we say about now, maybe being generous a year or so ago to get the game to where most were led to believe it should be and would have been at release.

CDPR conned the public, for financial gain, knowingly, and they squandered hundreds of thousands and likely millions actually on course correcting.

When all they had to do was not release the game until it was finished.

So whilst from what I witness every day in the industry I agree with your points as a whole, we shouldn’t give credit to what CDPR could do with a billion dollars, when the best example of what they did with less was verging on fraudulently selling and advertising a product, pulling it from sale, taking years to “fix” it and then regain consumer confidence.

Many may have forgiven and/or forgotten. They shouldn’t, and I sure won’t.

CDPR have a wonderful vision in their artistry, and I hope they go on to have success upon success. But what R* have achieved is miles beyond what many could achieve even with the money.

There’s numerous engines I’ve used over the years, entire workflows that quite literally can’t physically do what R* have pulled off with their team and technology. It needs really making clear to the laypeople of the world that this isn’t simply more money and talent, this is entirely new ways of approaching how to develop a game and how to use the the resources available.

CDPR literally looked at what they had, made mockups of ideas that were conceptual at best and ran with selling concept art that in some cases they still haven’t accomplished.

I don’t even have a history of playing a lot of R* content. But they have achieved something that money can’t currently buy. That’s the impressive part.

However, as stated, completely agree and disagree but not entirely. 😂 Peace and love on earth etc.

Totally agree, @ButteredCrumpet. I really don't understand where it all went so wrong with CDPR. The game looked immense before it was released, and I bought into it, yet we had all been conned. How on Earth did they think they could get away with it?

To be fair to them, they have righted the ship, and the game is completely different now to when it first launched, and I think what CPDR did has been a lesson from which the industry has (mostly!) learned (looking at you Mindseye!), and regardless of that I think that CPDR know more than anyone that all their future releases will be met with a degree of scepticism. @Fiendish-Beaver Absolutely agree. I believe in them, their talent and their capacity to deliver a game time and time again that is astounding.

Though I didn’t know of anyone on a personal level that worked on the project, it was clear early on something was not quite right with how the studio was handling things internally.

I even remember there being a time where more effort was seemingly being spent on a website, clues for the public and pre-rendered concept art than the game. As at that time they then claimed it was just a pipe dream of sorts.

Yet oddly one they were releasing next and seemingly had not even a mockup of a room or street lamp to speak of.

I personally think they got lost in the vision for a while, knowing as creatives they were onto something new and special. Almost like an artist staring at an oil painting for too long will always find a way to critique and amend it, yet not always objectively improve it.

I have now since gone back to Cyberpunk 2077 and though struggled at first to enjoy it, it has since clicked and I have had a wonderful time with it.

I think the biggest problem in development right now that I am witnessing first had, is simply too many suits trying to predict the next big thing, instead of allowing the next big thing to be naturally found.

Working in lighting and texturing, I can’t create the next big thing, I sort of have to discover it. But of course, that’s where the time and money element do apply. As without it I can’t excuse spending 6 months on a global sabbatical just meandering through the technology and discovering things on a whim.

It’s an odd industry really, it’s a lot like being a pop star, you’re told what to create, the timeline for when it’s expected to be completed, told how much will be charged for it, where and when it will be sold.

Yet you’re never really being told this by people who have much if any experience achieving it, so then you sit back and realise you may not be happy with something, but then my happiness with a texture doesn’t matter.

My happiness with the art I create matters only to the person viewing, yet the person that decides everything I create cares not for my happiness with it.

However, I’m only experiencing what many in and out of creative jobs experience. It’s not like it’s any different being told to move an Amazon parcel onto a conveyor and not wishing to.

I just sometimes wish we could all stop the conveyor and question why some things are being placed on it.

Art shouldn’t be rushed, as the historical examples people have provided on this site show, but then there is little to no industry without reliable performance, predictable results and financial investment.

In an ideal world art and money would never cross paths, but then tell that to Sotheby’s. An entire world of elitist ideals based on paintings by people who died financially bankrupt helping to prop up the wealth of the few.

Hardly what Rembrandt would have really wanted.

Thank you for your insight, @ButteredCrumpet. That was really interesting. Although not being able to paint or draw, nor hold a note or being computer literate, I do totally get what you mean about a creative starting at a canvas and seeing everything that they want to improve about the work they have done; about 25 to 30 years ago, I set about writing 3 novels. I finished two of them, and got part way through the third. The first two were in excess of 100,000 words, so these were not short stories. Problem is, I was forever going back through them and altering elements, and instead of shortening them, they would end up longer still, and I was always tinkering with them.

I often think about revisiting them as I never tried to get them published, but things changed for me when I met my second (now sadly deceased) wife. When I met her I dropped my writing, and even after her passing, I never returned to it, and instead fell headlong into gaming, and now I just cannot imagine spending long hours writing instead of gaming. Don't misunderstand me, I loved writing, and the writing process, but I think I probably enjoy gaming more, and so I'm not sure I'll return to it, but never say never, I guess...

@dark_knightmare2 It's a real shame that you're taking a celebration of what most believe is a landmark achievement in gaming and finding some way to be miserable about it. You're the guy at a baby shower talking about how the cake sucks.

@Fiendish-Beaver I am tremendously sorry to hear of the passing of your late wife that you experienced. Experiencing a great deal of loss myself, I know how much isn’t described by simply stating they are lost.

They’re there, in reverberations and memories at the very least, but grieving is a process I don’t believe fully ends, you sort of just learn to see things through another lens. Sometimes that is rose tinted and sometimes it’s darkness, but it’s always possible to see through them in time.

I won’t for a second try to tell you what to do, but maybe in time try to compel yourself to finish the writing, not in spite of all you experienced and how it changed you, but to have something you experienced change the way you write subconsciously and have it remembered forever.

When I lost my parents, I thought I’d change my career, I couldn’t create because all I could think of was the sheer volume of loss. How does one go about adding to the world when so focused on what has been taken from it.

Yet I found a way, I somehow found a way to regain a confidence not in myself, but in wanting to allow the light to win, and allow the work to speak of something I might not fully understand, but hopefully marks a time for someone out there that can gain from it.

Either way, you’re a creative with a story to tell. I for one would very much like to purchase anything literary you create no doubt.

Just remember, art knows no time, it’s there waiting for you if you ever find a moment.

I once tried to write a book on my dad’s typewriter, but then quickly learned it’s a very vulnerable process. Hence, I stopped, as vulnerability after a loss is never something one yearns for.

I think you will publish one day, the time will present itself, when it does, let me know. Who knows, it could help to heal another not just yourself.

In the meantime, gaming being your escapism only adds strings to your subconscious bow. If you ever need to scream or almost silently whisper, creative to creative, and grief exposed to another, you know where I am.

In a bizarre twist, Marvel fans think Doctor Doom goes with the Fantastic Four to pick up Steve Rogers in Avengers: Doomsday

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Doctor Doom is truly up to no good in Avengers: Doomsday, as Marvel fans think he has been edited out of a key scene in the final trailer.

One fan posted a screenshot over on Twitter of the part of the trailer where the Fantastic Four visit Steve Rogers at his house and ask for his help. But if you look closely, there is a rather large gap between Sue and Reed. Well, this fan seems to think that the movie's villain should be standing there. Check out the post below.

Marvel definitely edited Doctor Doom out of this scene in the trailer. https://t.co/Nn7baVBI1qNovember 23, 2026

You may be thinking, 'Wait, isn't Doom the baddie?' Why would the Fantastic Four bring him to Steve Rogers' house to ask for help defeating himself? You're right, as far as we know, Doom is the villain of the story. But many fans think he may have pulled the wool over a few heroes' eyes and is masking as a friend in order to infiltrate and destroy them.

We know that Doom has been collecting Marvel heroes ahead of Doomsday. Thanks to the VisionQuest finale, we know that Doom has already resurrected Scarlett Witch, and we saw the baddie kidnap Hulk during the Endgame Encore added footage. So, could this be Doom trying to enlist the Fantastic Four and Steve Rogers?

As the villain states in the bulk of Doomsday trailers, he has a personal vendetta against the Avengers due to the multiversal damage they caused, ultimately resulting in the loss of his family. And who contributed to that damage? Steve, when he flip-flopped between timelines, returning the Infinity Stones, before finally going back to the past to be with Peggy.

However, other fans think the person who has been edited out is actually Loki. This would make sense as we have already seen the God of Mischief visit Steve and Peggy at the end of Endgame Encore, setting up Doomsday. However, in the added footage, the duo are younger with a little baby, whereas in the trailer, the couple is found in a more modern setting with a grown child. Perhaps he has returned with the Fantastic Four to collect the second Steve – the one with long hair.

All will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday hits cinemas on December 18, and December 16 in the UK. For more, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline, and keep up with upcoming Marvel movies and shows on the way.

#3886. Archetype go all in on the Mass Effect vibes with a FemJun reveal, but I'm just left hoping they'll call the alternative option MascJun to balance it out

I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

To top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

It's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

#3885. Xbox Snags PS5 Exclusive 'Nioh 3' For January 2027 Release

Team NINJA's bloody samurai RPG features Xbox Play Anywhere

Xbox is bagging up former PlayStation exclusives like crazy, with Nioh 3 Complete Edition making its way to Xbox Series X|S on January 28, 2027.

Nioh follows Helldivers 2, the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy and PHYSINT by hopping aboard Xbox hardware. It's lovely to see renowned franchises like the dark samurai souls-like Nioh arrive on Xbox. It certainly beats seeing Halo and Gears launch on PS5 without anything major coming the other way.

Nioh 3 Complete Edition is an action RPG, in which players don the role of shogun Takechiyo, facing off against punishing soulslike scraps and challenges. Team NINJA shared a press release confirming the game is headed to Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox on January 28, 2027, complete with Xbox Play Anywhere support.

Nioh 3's second DLC, Bloody Insurrection, is set for December 17, 2026 for PS5 and Steam. The DLC will be included in the Complete Edition when it arrives early next year. As a franchise, Nioh has consistently wooed players with it's punishing combat and flashy action, with the third game holding an 86 on Metacritic.

Exciting times, eh? I wonder if this means Xbox players might gain access to Nioh 1 or 2 ports at some point in the future. Personally, I've always heard good things about the Nioh games, so it would be great to experience the entire series on Xbox, should Koei Tecmo make them available.

We'll leave you with an official description for the game along with some screenshots to look over:

Takechiyo must traverse time to change their fate and rescue a Japan overridden with yokai. Explore rich open fields and switch between Samurai and Ninja Styles instantaneously in battle. Encounter figures from history, and experience the tense battles characteristic of the Nioh series.

#3884. After GTA 6's original soundtrack, Justice probably won't work on any other video game ever again

You've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer. Featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and the fantastic King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, it's clear that the duo - and Rockstar - have spared no expense on the production of music for the game.

From what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City. You ought to enjoy the music while you can, though, because it seems Justice won't be coming back to video games any time soon. If ever.

Via a new interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project. "When [the offer to work with Rockstar] arrived on the table, we thought 'if there’s one video game we have to do, it's this one.' As soon as we accepted and started working [on the OST], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game."

Interesting. The duo, from the clip we can see on Rockyrama's posts, don't seem to give more information about this decision - did they have a bad time working with Rockstar? Was it intense? Or is it rather down to the fact that, if you're going to work on a game, you may as well make it what is largely expected to be the biggest game of all time.

Justice, for what it's worth, consider the work they've done on GTA 6 to be "a real album" of music - it's not seen as lesser or different to the band, just because it's being released as part of a video game. "GTA 6 gave us the excuse and direction to do it. The music always had to be listenable on its own, even if each track is tailored for [a specific] scene," the band explains.

The band's album isn't the only music connected to the game, either. There's also a 34-song album launching for the game, composed of original songs from some of the biggest artists in the world. The album features Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson and many more. The full tracklist leaked at the weekend.

GTA 6 launches on Thursday, 19th November for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week

#3883. Mondrayn is a putrid, crunchy pixel art RPG about escaping from limbo where "dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering"

Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

The world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

#3882. "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat" - Square Enix tempts Final Fantasy 14 players back with free game-time to fill void before new expansion

"People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons."

Final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February. So, in order to keep the game populated for the next few months, Square Enix is running a special promotion in hopes of tempting players back in.

This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies. Lapsed players who haven't logged in for over six months are to be given 30 days of free game time to hop back in and catch up with the main story quest ahead of Evercold's release.

In addition, there's an alluring character skip available too. If your FF14 character is at least level 90 on one class - the current level-cap is 100 - you can skip all the way to the final part of the latest Dawntrail expansion. You still need to grind to level 100 in preparation for Evercold, but the aforementioned free month of game time should provide plenty of time to do so.

In a producer letter written to accompany this promotion, Naoki Yoshida provided insight into why this was being implemented, stating that retaining players in an MMO like FF14 was of the "utmost importance".

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat", Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

"For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn launched, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today."

Yoshida went on to explain that promotions such as this are meant as a "tiny nudge". He notes that those who have retained subscriptions continuously remain "the most important" players in the development team's eyes, and acknowledges that the process of catching up in an MMO can seem "daunting" for many.

This problem of player retention is nothing new for MMOs, especially in the tricky time between the end of a current expansion and the beginning of a new one. MMO popularity often waxes and wanes, with a new expansion acting as an exciting call to action, with the months leading up to it often serving as a natural break-point for many. Still, monthly subs pay the bills, so keeping folks around even during these quiet months is important.

Final Fantasy 14: Evercold is looking like an especially exciting expansion. On top of the new story and two classes being added, the game is getting an overhaul to combat, with both classic Reborn and Evolved action modes, as well as a new raid difficulty meant to bridge the gap between normal and savage tiers.

The game has certainly come a long way since its initial release back in 2010. Dawntrail proved divisive among fans too, though with Evercold there's a lot of hope that a new overarching storyline can bring the steal back the hearts of players old and new.

You won't find the BF Bandito in a lock up in GTA 6, as this vehicle heist is a little tricker to pull off

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While you're out stealing cars for Moses, the GTA 6 BF Bandito will appear on your list, taking you out to the very rural roads of South Leonard County and the Buckskin Swamp. This GTA 6 heist is slightly harder than the others you might have carried out so far though, as this car will be on the move.Like all of Moses' targets, the rough location of the BF Bandito is marked on the map, but as you make your way there, you'll pass by some whoopin' and hollerin' country dwellers who are already taking the buggy for a spin. Here's how to get your hands on the GTA 6 Bandito and get paid.

The map marker will take you to the rough location of the BF Bandito, where you should keep your eyes and ears open for some locals riding around the swamps on buggies - one of these is the Bandito.

To claim it for yourself, you'll need to stop the Bandito driver, and there are a few ways to do this. If you clock him fast enough, particularly when crossing water, you can simply get in front of him, and he'll stop. Otherwise, you can chase down the Bandito, shooting the driver and his pals. Weirdly, though, when I did this challenge, the driver eventually just stopped and bolted, leaving the buggy free for me to take, though I'm not sure exactly what triggered him to do this. Essentially, just stay close, don't destroy the car by shooting it too much, and it'll be yours in no time.

If you're struggling to find some of the other GTA 6 cars that are ripe for the taking, then check I can also help you nab the Declasse Vamos, as well as Vanessa's cute GTA 6 pink Porsche - I mean, Pfister, which will be live shortly.

#3880. The siren call of user-generated content has caught Dead by Daylight in its snare, as Behaviour Interactive outline a big revamp update slated for next year

Weather, new models, better maps, it'll have it all

The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

"What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the plans for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely new modes, the possibilities are vast."

The post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a big visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial."

Beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big update sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

#3879. Is it time to retire Dragon Quest as a series? Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it might be

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death. The mangaka, whose art and distinct style were foundational to Chrono Trigger and Chrono Cross - and are still used in Dragon Quest to this day - died in 2024 at the age of 68.

Today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something new. This was all triggered by the announcement of Dragon Quest RPG: The Island of the Demon Tree and the Guided Island, an iOS and Android game that uses art that is very reminiscent of Toriyama's.

"The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," said Mitsuda. "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly new no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end for now, and [Dragon Quest creator, Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG. (There have been many remakes already.)"

Horii himself seems undeterred: with the new mobile game's announcement last week, he noted that the goal of his new project is to "capture that unmistakable Dragon Quest feeling" that comes with "exploring towns, meeting new allies, gearing up and steadily growing stronger". As Mitsuda calls for the series to retire, and for something new to take its place, Horii is keen to bring "the same classic adventure" to your smartphone.

"What's important is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future," concluded Mitsuda. "But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people."

It's unlikely Square Enix is going to want to drop the series, of course: the Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake exceeded Square Enix's (in)famously lofty expectations, and as the company aggressively pursues its multiplatform strategy, it's hard to imagine a world in which it's going to want to move away from a series that routinely pulls in millions of sales.

#3878. God of War Laufey Star Will Reprise Role for Live-Action TV Show

God of War Laufey’s lead Deborah Ann Woll will reprise her role as Kratos’ wife Faye in Amazon Prime’s upcoming live-action TV adaptation.

The actress – who also played the character in God of War Ragnarok – will star opposite Dave Bautista’s Kratos in the glitzy show.

The re-telling should end up feeling quite familiar, as Alastair Duncan will also return as Mimir.

Fans of the franchise will know Woll dies at the start of the story, kickstarting Kratos’ quest as he and son Atreus embark on a journey to scatter her ashes.

But we now know, during that period, Faye is trapped in a kind of afterlife for the gods known as the Everywhen. That’s where God of War Laufey will take place.

It’ll be interesting to see whether the TV show pulls in elements from the upcoming PS5 game, or if Woll’s role here will be to show Kratos’ family life prior to the events of the main game.

There’s no release date for the show just yet, but filming restarted in October with Baustita in the lead role, after previous actor Ryan Hurst was recast due to sustaining an injury on set.

Woll is an accomplished actress and knows the character inside-out, so this casting makes perfect sense to me.

#3877. GTA 6's Most Spectacular Easter Egg So Far Has Just Been Discovered

Update [Tue 24th Nov 2026, 2:27pm]: Our sister site Push Square has also now published a guide for this Easter Egg:

Guide GTA 6: Vice City Easter Egg Walkthrough & Tommy Vercetti Shirt Unlock

Push SquareFind the portal and get your Tommy Vercetti rewards

Original Story: One of the coolest things about GTA 6 since release has been watching players discover all kinds of Easter Eggs, such as the Mario-inspired hats that were shared by our sister site Nintendo Life yesterday.

We reckon this is the best one so far though - a secret portal that takes you into a nightclub from the original 2002 version of Vice City for the PS2 (which technically means it takes you back to its 1986-inspired setting).

The process of getting here is long-winded, and detailed in full in the video from Dan Allen Gaming up above. In a nutshell, you have to go to the Badger R&D Radio Tower in Key Lento and use the power switch and press a button to make the Malibu logo appear on the TV. From there, visit 12 LPL substations around the map without fast-travelling, and press the correct buttons in the specific order (from the video) when you reach them. You'll then get a text, at which point you head to Reactor 2 at the LPL Turtle Head Power Station between 7pm and 6am to find the portal.

It seems someone called Memelo was the first to discover this trick:

Another really cool part of this Easter Egg is that when you combine all the substations together, the wording on the outside of them adds up to "Life is Passing Me By", which references a classic cheat code from the original Vice City. You actually have to use the buttons to enter this cheat code and make the portal appear.

As mentioned, you get two free items for your trouble as well, which are Tommy Vercetti's classic shirt and bike from the 2002 game. These appear as soon as you're thrown out of the portal and back into the so-called real world!

Finally, we'll also highlight that although pretty much all the footage we've seen of this Easter Egg has been exclusive to the Jason character, it does appear to work with Lucia as well. That said, we've also come across many players who claim the portal isn't showing up for them, so we're not sure what's causing it to fail in those situations.

Anyway, crazy stuff right?! Who knows what other insane Easter Eggs might be discovered over the coming days and weeks - some people have mentioned they're seeing a "flashback" pop-up after completing the Vice City one, with a suggestion there may be another four flashback sequences yet to be found. Let's hope so!

#3876. Slow down a bit and help a cow find a friend in the lush-looking, hand-drawn, milk deliver-em-up Milki Delivery, which is out now

I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

It's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

#3875. Call of Duty might have swapped guns and tanks for knights and swords if an Infinity Ward experiment had panned out

"If it's a war story, sure, it can be COD."

As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold new directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day. And it turns out a medieval Call of Duty was also explored at one time.

This latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game. "Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right?" Kurosaki told PC Gamer. "It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty."

This isn't the first time we've heard of an unusual Call of Duty prototype. When Activision brought Sledgehammer Games into the fold as another lead studio for the lucrative shooter series, the team briefly worked on a third-person horror off-shoot set in Vietnam, which was referred to as Fog of War.

Activision's legal battle with Infinity Ward founders Vince Zampella and Jason West, however, caused the project to be cancelled, as Sledgehammer was roped into helping the studio finish Modern Warfare 3.

As for Kurosaki, he currently leads That's No Moon alongside creative partner Jacob Minkoff and other Infinity Ward and Naughty Dog veterans. The studio is currently working on Crossfire, a narrative-driven third-person shooter set in the universe of Smilegate's free-to-play series of the same name.

The companies are old friends in the industry

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Remakes of the first two Max Payne games are on the way, and Rockstar's been helping Remedy get the releases in order. According to the Control and Alan Wake studio, collaborating with the purveyor of GTA 6 has been absolutely grand so far.

Jean-Charles Gaudechon, the CEO of Remedy, described the working relationship between the two outfits in glowing terms for Game File. "Honestly, it's been great," he says. "You know why? Because I think they're super respectful of Remedy."

Respect is a good start to any collaboration. Gaudechon then doubles down, just to make it clear everything's positive right now. "I'll say it out loud: They've honestly been an awesome partner," he adds. "And it's no bullshit."

Well, it seems he doesn't have any complaints, anyway. Remedy and Rockstar actually have quite a bit of history, since the studio that gave us GTA actually worked on ports of the first Max Payne, then published the second outright.

It only makes sense, then, that they'd team back up to give both games a lick of paint and update them for modern hardware. As you may well be aware, it's been a while since Rockstar's done anything outside of the Grand Theft Auto or Red Dead Redemption mines.

Time was the developer and publisher would be involved in all sorts of projects, but nowadays the focus tends to be a little more streamlined. I guess that's what happens when you make the biggest games in the industry.

The two have been working on these do-overs since around 2022, and we don't have a release window yet. Perhaps now that Alan Wake 2 and Control: Resonant are out of the way, Remedy can put in more resource, while Rockstar can finally do something that isn't GTA 6. I mean, how much is there to do post-launch for such a game? Our boy Max is waiting, people – come on.

#3872. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is the US' best-selling physical game so far this year

The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game, Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail.

The remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom. That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years.

While Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026, and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028.

Ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post, Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

#3871. Ex-Nvidia boss Jensen Huang offers to return if that's best for the company and America, Nvidia board essentially say 'nah, we're all good'

New rulers impervious to highly persuasive message of 'come on, please give me my job back, go USA'

Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.

"On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

That last bit seems likely to have been said with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

"Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO."

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board announced yesterday that they're establishing a "new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is currently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the company's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

#3870. Quantum Break Developer Responds To Sequel Demand For The 2016 Xbox Exclusive

"We love the amount of love for the game"

It's been 10 years since Quantum Break made its debut as an Xbox console exclusive in 2016, and Xbox fans have often considered it somewhat of an underated cult classic from the developer behind the likes of Control and Alan Wake.

So, could we get a sequel?! Remedy Entertainment's X account has been talking about this over the last 24 hours, highlighting that the team love how much passion fans still have for the IP, but that the decision is in Xbox's hands.

In other words, it's down to Asha Sharma and her group at Xbox HQ.

Now, to be honest, we don't reckon it's a likely bet. The original Quantum Break was a really cool exclusive for Xbox to have 10 years ago, but it seems like the new Xbox CEO is more interested in focusing on big franchises like Gears, Halo, Fallout and The Elder Scrolls rather than dipping back into something from a difficult period in Xbox's history.

That's not to say it couldn't happen though, and in some ways you'd think it'd be an easy win for Xbox to cater to nostalgia and remind everyone how much they enjoyed the original Quantum Break. Remedy has made sequels to Alan Wake and Control in recent times as well, so they'd surely be up for revisiting QB if given the opportunity.

What do you think, should Xbox greenlight a new Quantum Break game? Let us know in the poll and comments below.

#3869. Sci-fi RPG Exodus continues evoking Mass Effect by revealing female lead and nicknaming her FemJun

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

Is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

There are, however, big and important differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

Archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons company Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

Archetype announced a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

Matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year."

#3868. Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

Administrators say "a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise"

Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it says on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Announced in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

The same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The company grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "currently engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

The first set of GTA 6 patch notes are here, with a post-launch update arriving on November 23. But let me temper your expectations as this patch isn't anything particularly interesting unless you've been affected by any of the bugs and crashes that the patch aims to iron out. There are hardly going to be any substantial changes to the game less than a week after launch, but I've laid out the Xbox and PS5 patch notes for GTA 6 below.

You can read the full notes for GTA 6's first post-launch update on Rockstar's support website, but they're so short that I've laid them all out below:

As you can see, there are only seven fixes, all of which are for high-priority gameplay issues, such as crashes, problems with the autosave system, and not receiving mission-critical phone calls for progression. While the autosave system should hopefully be working as intended, it still helps to know how to save in GTA 6 so that you can manually bank your progress. And for the latter point about phone calls, many of them just require you to pass the time by doing other activities to trigger, like when you meet Halifax as part of the GTA 6 Dubious Provenance mission in Chapter 3.

If you've been affected by any of these, make sure you get the patch installed and you should be able to carry on playing and making progress through the main story – though if you need some help, our GTA 6 guides are all here.

#3866. PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

12.2 million gamers can be wrong, apparently.

Sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness). The judgment came after a 30-day Competition Appeal Tribunal that took place in London, where PlayStation users claimed Sony had removed "all actual and potential competition" in relation to selling digital games on the console.

The case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store. In a judgment published by the London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today (17th November), the case was rejected. The judgement noted that market definitions used to define Sony's conduct were "unsafe", and that consumers "would be likely to make informed choices when purchasing consoles" and games on the hardware, too.

"Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.

The lawsuit made the argument that, upon purchasing a PS5 or other PlayStation console, you were then trapped within its ecosystem, and forced into paying the prices determined by Sony. The Tribunal disagreed, however, and ruled that Sony competed within a wider 'systems market' alongside Xbox, Nintendo and PC, for example. Furthermore, the Tribunal found no evidence that the existence of other digital storefronts would have actually brought any PlayStation Store pricing down.

Interestingly, the Tribunal used the argument that consumers can also opt and buy physical games instead of using the PlayStation Store - something that is changing as of the start of 2028. That did not seem to have any bearing on today's decision, though. It's also worth noting that this case did not seek to interrogate the ownership status of digital games - something that's been at the heart of the movement rallying against Sony's decision to kill off physical media. Earlier this year, spokespeople from Sony's legal team argued "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games.

The London Tribunal has a fairly long history. Back in 2022, it began as a case that attempted to sue Sony to the tune of £5bn for "ripping people off" on PlayStation Store. Sony argued the case brought against it in this trial was "flawed from start to finish". This isn't the only situation where we're seeing consumers pursue legal action against the platform holder. Last year, PlayStation was sued in the Netherlands over the so-called "Sony tax" that highlighted artificially inflated prices on the Store, and sought to represent more than 20,000 participants that felt short-changed by the company.

#3865. Today Is Your Last Chance to Play Destruction AllStars on PS5

Forgotten car combat game Destruction AllStars has been in some stage of extinction for years now, but if you do have the PS5 game in your library, then today truly is the last day you can play it in any meaningful manner.

From tomorrow, 25th November 2026, the last of its game services will be taken offline.

The multiplayer servers were already permanently pulled in May 2026, and within the next 24 hours, "all remaining game services will be taken offline", per communication from Sony.

Single player modes had still been available to play, but those will be removed too when their servers are taken offline.

Quite literally the only content left in Destruction AllStars after tomorrow is an arcade mode and challenges. Even then, though, Sony warns the "functionality and player experience" tied to that content could be impacted.

Basically, if you want to experience even a sliver of the Destruction AllStars experience, you've only got today left to do it. It's already been delisted from the PS Store, so if you don't have a copy now, you're completely out of luck.

It's not like you'd be missing out on much, to be fair.

Destruction AllStars never made a splash in terms of quality or popularity. While it did have a small playerbase during its days with active servers, the game quickly died out after a February 2021 release.

Will you be playing Destruction AllStars one last time today? Let us know in the comments below.

[source News: PS5's Destruction AllStars Delisted and Disabled Without Notice Due to 'Ongoing Technical Issues']

#3864. GTA 6 Comparison Reveals Two Advantages Of Xbox Series X Over PS5

The good folks over at Digital Foundry are still busy analysing all things to do with GTA 6's launch last week, and their latest comparison takes a look at all four console versions alongside each other - Series X, S, PS5 and PS5 Pro.

They also go on to rank the versions in order, and perhaps surprisingly, Xbox Series X comes out on top versus the standard PS5. Two reasons are given for this, which are that the Xbox version supports 120Hz VRR to smooth out the dips in frame rate, and that the PS5 sometimes "suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X".

"Although both target 30fps and maintain it during typical gameplay, heavy vehicle traversal and intense airport crowd sequences cause frame-rates to drop into the mid to upper 20s. PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips. Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off."

Visually, there are said to be no real differences between the Xbox Series X and PS5 versions, although the Series X version does have "slightly more pronounced heat haze effects in one opening shot".

All of this is obviously beaten by the PS5 Pro though, which is said to "deliver the definitive console GTA 6 experience by leveraging its larger GPU, accelerated machine learning hardware and enhanced ray tracing features".

"Overall, the PS5 Pro leads the rankings with its superior visual detail and rock-solid 30fps target, followed by the Xbox Series X - which edges out the standard PS5 through better performance stability. The Xbox Series S sits at the bottom due to visual trade-offs, unstable frame-rates and audio glitches."

It's fair to say we never expected the Xbox Series X version to fare better than the PS5 version in this case, especially considering all the "plays best on PS5" marketing that surrounded GTA 6 prior to release.

Of course, Digital Foundry seeks out the most minute of details when it comes to technical analysis, and the differences between the Xbox Series X and standard PS5 versions aren't going to be major enough to suggest one version is far better than another. It's just interesting that they've ended up ranking the Series X higher in this instance.

Let us hear your thoughts in the comments, but please do keep it respectful! We enjoy the PS5 as well, and know plenty of people who are loving the game on that system. All the same, this is a fascinating analysis and a bonus for Xbox.

#3863. PC remains GTA 6's last hope for 60fps smoothness as Rockstar confirm such an option isn't coming to even the swankiest consoles

Poor little game boxes just can't handle it

As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates."

So, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

#3862. The Game Awards just confirmed who plays GTA 6's Lucia

Manni L. Perez has been confirmed as the actress behind Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos, just days before the game launches.

As spotted by IGN, the confirmation came during The Game Awards' nominations livestream today, where Perez was nominated for Best Performance for her role as co-lead Lucia.

Perez had been widely rumoured to play Lucia for months, and fans have regularly filled her social media livestreams with questions about GTA 6, which she has been oh-so-carefully sidestepping.

Lucia is one half of GTA 6's lead pair alongside Jason Duval, making it the first Grand Theft Auto game with a playable couple.

Jason's actor wasn't among the nominees, so who plays him is still a mystery.

Perez has previously had guest roles in a string of US TV dramas, including Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago P.D., The Blacklist, and Blindspot, and has also done voice work for GTA Online.

Funnily enough, Lucia isn't her first Lucia - she also played Lucia Santiago in a 2023 episode of CBS's East New York.

GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

It's long been revealed that GTA 6 will have a regional release, meaning that some lucky, soon-to-be players will be able to access the game much earlier than others. Rockstar's regional release schedule sees the game launching at midnight on 19th November regardless of what region you're in, and if you wish to join those playing almost a day early, there's the good ol' Xbox New Zealand trick for eager players to try.

#3861. Chronicles: Medieval devs Raw Power are bankrupt, but their sandbox RPG lives on at a new studio co-founded by Satisfactory devs Coffee Stain

It "ticks many of the boxes", despite the funding problems

Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

The original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

Raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

Gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the new team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.
